advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Restore the LIVE-mode pre/post ticket-id diff (e.g. difflib.unified_diff over pre_ids/post) to stderr so a store-differs warning names the specific tickets.
evidence: Port: `print("\n\033[31mWARNING: live store differs after cleanup!\033[0m", file=sys.stderr)` at scripts/probe_rebar.py:247 — no diff of the differing id sets is emitted.
Deleted shell original emitted the detail: `diff <(printf '%s' "$_PRE_IDS") <(printf '%s' "$post") >&2 || true` (see removed cleanup() in scripts/probe-rebar.sh diff).
Both `pre_ids` and `post` are newline-joined id strings available in _cleanup (scripts/probe_rebar.py:243 `post = _ticket_dirs(tracker)`), so the diff can be reconstructed.
advisory.finding: In PROBE_LIVE mode, the Python cleanup drops the shell's diagnostic diff of pre/post ticket-id sets. The shell printed `diff <(printf '%s' "$_PRE_IDS") <(printf '%s' "$post")` to stderr on divergence; the port prints only a generic 'live store differs' warning, so an operator can no longer see WHICH tickets leaked or were removed.
scenarios: A PROBE_LIVE=1 run against the real project store where cleanup fails to fully restore the ticket set — the operator sees a warning but must manually enumerate the store to find the leaked/removed tickets.
advisory.suggested_fix: In _cleanup's else branch, additionally print the symmetric difference, e.g. `import difflib; sys.stderr.write(''.join(difflib.unified_diff(pre_ids.splitlines(keepends=True), post.splitlines(keepends=True), 'pre','post')))`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an automated test (or a CI step) that runs `PROBE_INJECT_FAIL=1 python scripts/probe_rebar.py` in isolated mode and asserts it exits non-zero AND that the summary reports a non-zero failed count with later sections still executed, so the continue-on-failure invariant is gated.
evidence: scripts/probe_rebar.py:8-11 docstring: 'CONTINUE-ON-FAILURE IS THE DESIGN ... The harness exits non-zero iff any assertion failed. Do not convert assertion helpers to raise.'
search_files for 'PROBE_INJECT_FAIL' returns only scripts/probe_rebar.py:24 (docstring) and :255 (the branch); search_files for 'INJECT_FAIL' under .github returns no matches — no workflow invokes it
CI invokes the probe only in the happy path: test.yml:128 and gerrit-verify.yaml:209 both run `python scripts/probe_rebar.py </dev/null` with no PROBE_INJECT_FAIL

Ticket f1eb Testing section names this as the verification: 'inject one failing probe -> harness continues, reports it, exits non-zero' — asserted manually in a comment, not gated by any automated test
ABSENCE: no test under tests/ exercises probe_rebar.py; search_files for 'probe_rebar' shows only the anti-rot wiring test, which checks the workflow string, not the harness behavior
advisory.finding: The continue-on-failure + non-zero-exit contract — the central invariant this port preserves — has a purpose-built self-test mode (PROBE_INJECT_FAIL=1) that no automated test or CI step ever invokes, so a regression converting an assertion helper to raise (which the docstring explicitly forbids) would not be caught by any gate.
scenarios: A future refactor makes _fail() or an assertion helper raise; _probe() aborts at the first failure and skips all later sections, masking regressions the probe is meant to surface — no automated gate flags the change in behavior.
The self-test branch itself silently rots (e.g. the injected needle stops failing) and no test notices.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add tests/unit/test_probe_selftest.py that invokes the probe as a subprocess with PROBE_INJECT_FAIL=1 and REBAR pointed at the installed binary (skip/xfail with a concrete env-guard when rebar isn't installed), asserting returncode == 1 and that stdout contains 'PROBE RESULT:' with '1 failed' plus a late-section marker (e.g. the 'delete — friction' section header) to prove the run continued past the injected failure.
